hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 adheres more tightly to some recycling receptors than APOE3, impeding recycling.

paper.title: Decreased lipidated ApoE-receptor interactions confer protection against pathogenicity of ApoE and its lipid cargoes in lysosomes.

findings.finding_description: Surface plasmon resonance measured binding of POPC-lipidated ApoE isoforms to the purified LDLR extracellular domain. lipApoE4 had a KD of 9 nM and lipApoE3 16 nM, both high affinity, while lipApoE2 was about 50-fold weaker (800 nM).
findings.quote: SPR similarly revealed a high affinity LDLR binding for both lipApoE4 and lipApoE3 (KD = 9 nM and 16 nM, respectively), whereas the lipApoE2-LDLR affinity was ~50-fold lower than lipApoE3 (KD = 800 nM; Figure 1D).
findings.summary: By SPR, lipApoE4 bound the LDLR ECD slightly more tightly than lipApoE3 (KD 9 vs 16 nM); lipApoE2 binding was far weaker.
findings.experimental_system: Cell-free SPR: HEK293-derived recombinant POPC-lipidated ApoE isoforms with recombinant human LDLR extracellular domain

findings.finding_description: HTRF measured binding of lipApoE isoforms to the LDLR ECD. lipApoE3 and lipApoE4 showed similar high-affinity binding (EC50 ~13 nM each), with no E4 vs E3 difference, while lipApoE2 showed minimal binding. This is a null result for the E4 > E3 binding claim.
findings.quote: Conversely, lipApoE3 and lipApoE4 both exhibited high affinity binding, demonstrating a half maximum effective concentration (EC50) of ~13 nM.
findings.summary: By HTRF, lipApoE3 and lipApoE4 bound LDLR with equal apparent affinity (EC50 ~13 nM).
findings.experimental_system: Cell-free HTRF: recombinant lipidated ApoE isoforms with LDLR extracellular domain

findings.finding_description: Cell-surface LDLR was immunostained after 1 d of lipApoE treatment. lipApoE3/E4 significantly reduced surface LDLR relative to lipApoE2 in H4 neuroglioma cells, HAP1 cells and APOE KO iPSC-derived astrocytes, which the authors interpret as impaired recycling. No ApoE4 vs ApoE3 difference is reported.
findings.quote: In H4, WT HAP1, and APOE KO iAstrocytes, incubation with lipApoE3/E4 significantly reduced surface LDLR relative to lipApoE2, revealing impaired LDLR recycling accompanying increased LDLR-mediated lipApoE uptake
findings.summary: lipApoE3 and lipApoE4 both reduced surface LDLR (a proxy for impaired recycling) versus lipApoE2 in human brain-derived cells; no E4 > E3 difference is stated.
findings.experimental_system: Human H4 neuroglioma cells, WT HAP1 cells, and human APOE KO iPSC-derived astrocytes treated with exogenous lipApoE

findings.finding_description: Super-resolution imaging of APOE KO iAstrocytes showed internalized lipApoE fully colocalized with endogenous LDLR for all isoforms, mostly inside LAMP1 compartments. Internalized ApoE followed ApoE4 > ApoE3 > ApoE2, as did the fraction of LAMP1 vesicles containing ApoE (0.497 vs 0.410 vs 0.266).
findings.quote: ApoE isoform differences were manifested in the differential levels of internalized lipApoE (ApoE4 > ApoE3 > ApoE2), giving rise to the same isoform trend for LAMP1-positive vesicles containing ApoE immunoreactivity (Mander’s coefficients = 0.266 ± 0.045 for ApoE2, 0.410 ± 0.049 for ApoE3, 0.497 ± 0.090 for ApoE4)
findings.summary: In human iAstrocytes, more ApoE4 than ApoE3 was internalized and retained with LDLR in LAMP1 compartments, consistent with receptor trapping.
findings.experimental_system: Human APOE KO iPSC-derived astrocytes treated with lipApoE isoforms, super-resolution imaging

findings.finding_description: Immunostaining in lipApoE-treated H4 cells showed cell-associated ApoE extensively colocalized with LDLR puncta outside transferrin-labeled recycling endosomes. This suggests LDLR is trapped by ApoE in other endolysosomal compartments rather than recycled; the isoform comparison is not specified in the text.
findings.quote: Cell-associated ApoE immunoreactivity extensively colocalized with LDLR puncta (Figure 2G) outside of transferrin-labeled recycling endosomes (Figure S2D), suggesting “trapping” of LDLR by ApoE in other endolysosomal compartments.
findings.summary: Internalized ApoE stayed bound to LDLR outside recycling endosomes, suggesting the receptor is trapped instead of recycled.
findings.experimental_system: Human H4 neuroglioma cells treated with lipApoE3/E4

findings.finding_description: DiI-LDL uptake was measured in serum-starved H4 cells as a functional readout of LDLR availability. Co-treatment with lipApoE3 or lipApoE4 inhibited uptake by 60–65%, and 1 d pretreatment nearly abolished it, while lipApoE2 had no effect or modestly enhanced uptake. No E4 vs E3 difference is reported.
findings.quote: When cells were co-treated with lipApoE and DiI-LDL for 3–4 h, both lipApoE3 and lipApoE4 led to 60–65% inhibition of DiI-LDL uptake, likely via a direct competition with LDL for LDLR binding, whereas lipApoE2 had no effect (Figure 2J, L). When DiI-LDL was spiked into media after 1d pre-treatment with lipApoE3/E4, DiI-LDL uptake was nearly abolished
findings.summary: lipApoE3 and lipApoE4 similarly suppressed LDLR-mediated LDL uptake in H4 cells, consistent with LDLR sequestration without an E4 > E3 difference.
findings.experimental_system: Human H4 neuroglioma cells

findings.finding_description: Total LDLR immunostaining in H4 cells after lipApoE3/E4 treatment showed a modest but significant reduction, with signals that appeared slightly more clustered.
findings.quote: Immunostaining of total LDLR (cell surface + intracellular) in H4 cells after lipApoE3/E4 treatment showed a modest but significant reduction in signals, which also appeared slightly more clustered (Figure 2E–F).
findings.summary: lipApoE3/E4 modestly reduced and clustered total LDLR in H4 cells.
findings.experimental_system: Human H4 neuroglioma cells

findings.finding_description: In a cell-based binding assay, FITC-labeled lipApoE was incubated at 4°C with 293T cells overexpressing human LDLR. lipApoE3 and lipApoE4 both gave robust surface signals and lipApoE2 minimal signal. The system is non-brain, and no E4 vs E3 difference is described.
findings.quote: Robust cell surface signals were observed for lipApoE3 and lipApoE4, while minimal signals were observed for lipApoE2, indicating reduced binding of lipApoE2 to LDLR (Figure 1A–B).
findings.summary: In LDLR-overexpressing 293T cells, lipApoE3 and lipApoE4 bound robustly; lipApoE2 barely bound.
findings.experimental_system: 293T cells overexpressing human LDLR, 4°C binding assay
findings.needs_review: strength 4 -> 2: no surrogate at either end (direct LDLR binding assay); weakness is relevance (293T cells, no E4-vs-E3 difference), not link strength

findings.finding_description: pHrodo-lipApoE uptake in human APOE KO iAstrocytes showed the same isoform trend as in HAP1 cells, where lipApoE2 uptake was lower than lipApoE3/E4. Blocking with the LDLR ECD abolished the trend, implicating LDLR as the receptor.
findings.quote: Lastly, in human APOE KO iPSC-derived astrocytes (iAstrocytes), pHrodo-lipApoE uptake showed similar isoform trend that was abolished by blocking uptake of lipApoE3/E4 with LDLR ECD (Figure S1I–J), validating findings in a CNS cell type.
findings.summary: LDLR-dependent ApoE uptake in human astrocytes was higher for E3/E4 than E2.
findings.experimental_system: Human APOE KO iPSC-derived astrocytes

findings.finding_description: qPCR in APOE KO iAstrocytes showed LDLR mRNA was upregulated by all lipApoE isoforms. Yet only lipApoE3/E4 failed to raise surface LDLR, which the authors attribute to impaired recycling rather than reduced expression.
findings.quote: While all 3 ApoE isoforms impacted LDLR mRNA levels, lipApoE3/E4 abrogated the expected increase in surface LDLR by impairing its recycling.
findings.summary: Reduced surface LDLR with E3/E4 is not explained by lower LDLR transcription in iAstrocytes.
findings.experimental_system: Human APOE KO iPSC-derived astrocytes

findings.finding_description: Quantitative direct binding assays of POPC-lipidated ApoE isoforms to the LDLR extracellular domain showed a ~50–100-fold lower LDLR-binding affinity for ApoE2 than for ApoE3 or ApoE4, and a comparable binding affinity between ApoE3 and ApoE4.
findings.quote: Using quantitative, direct binding assays, we demonstrated a ~50–100-fold decrease in LDLR-binding affinity for ApoE2 vs. ApoE3/E4 and a comparable binding affinity for ApoE3 and ApoE4.
findings.summary: Lipidated ApoE3 and ApoE4 bind LDLR with comparable affinity; ApoE2 binds much more weakly.
findings.experimental_system: HEK293-purified POPC-lipidated ApoE, in vitro HTRF LDLR-binding assay

findings.finding_description: In most cellular uptake assays, lipApoE4 was only minimally differentiated from lipApoE3; the observed isoform-dependent effects were largely driven by ApoE2’s weaker receptor binding rather than by a difference between ApoE3 and ApoE4.
findings.quote: ApoE isoform-dependent receptor binding could only explain protective mechanism of ApoE2, with ApoE4 minimally differentiated from ApoE3 in most uptake assays
findings.summary: Lipidated ApoE4 was not markedly higher than ApoE3 in receptor-mediated uptake assays.
findings.experimental_system: multiple human cellular models

findings.finding_description: In several human cell models, LDLR-mediated uptake of lipApoE3 and lipApoE4 caused endolysosomal trapping of LDLR and depletion of cell surface LDLR, further reducing LDL uptake; lipApoE2 did not produce these effects because of its defective LDLR binding.
findings.quote: LDLR-mediated uptake of lipApoE3 and lipApoE4 led to endolysosomal trapping of LDLR and depletion of cell surface LDLR, resulting in further reduced LDL uptake. LipApoE2 did not show these effects due to defective LDLR binding.
findings.summary: Lipidated ApoE3 and ApoE4 similarly trap LDLR in endolysosomes and deplete surface LDLR, whereas ApoE2 does not.
findings.experimental_system: multiple human cellular models

findings.finding_description: Exogenous pHrodo green-labeled lipidated ApoE isoforms (~294 nM) were added to human cells (H4, HAP1 lines, APOE KO iPSC-derived astrocytes), and cellular uptake into acidic compartments was imaged live. The authors note that ApoE4 vs. ApoE3 uptake efficiency varied with lipidation batch, but the overall trend was ApoE4 >= ApoE3 > ApoE2. This is a surrogate (uptake) for receptor binding and says nothing directly about recycling.
findings.quote: The exact uptake efficiency of ApoE4 vs. ApoE3 varies across different lipidation batches, but an overall trend of ApoE4 >= ApoE3 > ApoE2 was observed.
findings.summary: Across human cell lines and iAstrocytes, lipidated ApoE4 uptake was equal to or greater than ApoE3, though the result was batch-variable and is only a surrogate for receptor binding.
findings.experimental_system: Human H4 neuroglioma cells, HAP1 cells, and APOE KO iPSC-derived human astrocytes treated with exogenous pHrodo-labeled lipidated recombinant ApoE isoforms
findings.data_location: STAR Methods, pHrodo-lipApoE uptake assay (methods statement; no figure panel given in excerpt)

findings.finding_description: Surface LDLR immunostaining was done in HAP1 cells after 1 d with POPC-lipidated ApoE. The legend title reports that both lipidated ApoE3 and ApoE4, but not LDL, sequester LDLR. Specific isoform comparisons and their statistics are only in the figure.
findings.quote: Figure S2. Lipidated ApoE3 and ApoE4, but not LDL, sequester LDLR, related to Figure 2 (A) Confocal images of cell surface LDLR staining for HAP1 cells after 1 d incubation with 10 μg/mL POPC-lipidated ApoE.
findings.summary: Lipidated ApoE3 and ApoE4 both sequester LDLR away from the cell surface in HAP1 cells, so sequestration is not stated to be ApoE4-specific.
findings.experimental_system: HAP1 human cell line (non-brain) treated with recombinant POPC-lipidated ApoE isoforms

findings.finding_description: In H4 neuroglioma cells, ApoE and LDLR were co-immunostained after 1 d of POPC-lipidated ApoE4, with a transferrin pulse to label recycling endosomes. This only describes ApoE4 localization relative to recycling endosomes. It is class 5 because only ApoE4 was tested, with no ApoE3 comparison, so the cause is not varied and no quantification is given.
findings.quote: (D) Confocal images for co-immunostaining of ApoE and LDLR in H4 cells after 1 d treatment with 10 μg/mL POPC-lipidated ApoE4 followed by 15 min incubation with Alexa 488-labeled Transferrin to label recycling endosomes.
findings.summary: ApoE4 and LDLR localization was imaged against transferrin-labeled recycling endosomes in H4 cells, with ApoE4 only.
findings.experimental_system: H4 human neuroglioma cells treated with POPC-lipidated ApoE4

findings.finding_description: Uptake of pHrodo-labeled POPC-lipidated ApoE isoforms was measured in APOE KO iPSC-derived astrocytes, with and without LDLR extracellular domain competitor. This tests whether isoform-dependent uptake is LDLR-mediated, a surrogate for receptor engagement.
findings.quote: (I) Confocal images of pHrodo green-labeled POPC-lipidated ApoE (used at 10 μg/mL) detected in APOE KO iAstrocytes after 1 d incubation, with and without co-treatment of 20 μg/mL LDLR ECD.
findings.summary: In human iAstrocytes, ApoE isoform uptake was probed for LDLR dependence by LDLR ECD competition.
findings.experimental_system: APOE KO human iPSC-derived astrocytes treated with recombinant lipidated ApoE isoforms

findings.finding_description: Cellular uptake of pHrodo-labeled lipidated ApoE isoforms was measured in H4 cells, with and without LDLR ECD or heparin. Uptake is reported as ApoE isoform-dependent, which is a surrogate for differential receptor binding.
findings.quote: Figure S1. ApoE isoform-dependent cellular uptake of POPC-lipidated ApoE, related to Figure 1
findings.summary: Uptake of lipidated ApoE differs by isoform and is probed with LDLR ECD and heparin competition.
findings.experimental_system: H4 human neuroglioma cells; WT, LDLR KO and LRP1 KO HAP1 cells

findings.finding_description: A cell-free HPLC heparin-column binding assay compared retention times of non-lipidated ApoE isoforms. Heparin binding stands in for receptor/HSPG affinity; no cells and no recycling were measured.
findings.quote: (A) HPLC profiles for non-lipidated ApoE isoforms eluted from a heparin column in a representative HPLC-based heparin binding experiment, with average retention time from 3 independent experiments indicated for individual isoforms.
findings.summary: Heparin-binding affinity of ApoE isoforms was compared in a cell-free assay.
findings.experimental_system: Cell-free recombinant non-lipidated ApoE isoforms on a heparin HPLC column

findings.finding_description: qPCR of 3 genes was performed in APOE KO iAstrocytes after 1 d of lipidated ApoE isoform treatment, as part of the LDLR sequestration figure. The genes and results are not given in the text.
findings.quote: (C) Relative expression of 3 genes quantified by qPCR for APOE KO iAstrocytes after 1 d treatment with 10 μg/mL POPC-lipidated ApoE (n = 3 independent experiments).
findings.summary: Transcriptional readout in iAstrocytes after ApoE isoform treatment, presented alongside LDLR sequestration.
findings.experimental_system: APOE KO human iPSC-derived astrocytes
